name: Define document-centric To-TRD lifecycle
description: Define a governed redesign of the To-TRD lifecycle so it tracks the state of the TRD document itself rather than implementation of the requirements. Replace the current not_done semantics with a TRD-complete state, keep implementation progress in the separate implementation-plan and Task systems, establish migration and compatibility rules, and capture the result in a managed TRD without implementing the redesign.
definition_of_done: The active and reusable To-TRD packages, helper lifecycle schema, tests, documentation, current TRD catalog, and To-Implementation-Plan handoff contract are inspected as current sources.
The user confirms the exact canonical and user-facing lifecycle vocabulary, including the replacement for not_done and the meaning of draft, TRD completion, and retirement.
The requirements define clear ownership boundaries: To-TRD tracks document completion, while implementation-plan and Task systems track planned and performed implementation work.
The requirements define how existing TRD records, indexes, commands, tests, documentation, reusable and active packages, and downstream consumers migrate without silently corrupting state.

A managed project-local TRD is created through the To-TRD helper with source-linked requirements, observable acceptance criteria, explicit exclusions, Open questions set to None, and no unresolved ambiguity disguised as downstream instructions.
No To-TRD implementation, existing-record migration, dependency installation, destructive operation, Git action, publication, or deployment is performed under this requirements-definition Task.
current_summary: TASK-20260904-9702FDD5 is complete. TRD-20260904-E2BADD07 revision 3 is the user-approved requirements baseline for a document-centric To-TRD lifecycle using draft, trd_done, and retired. Its legacy frontmatter remains draft by explicit user authorization until a separately planned and authorized implementation migrates it. No package implementation, existing-record migration, dependency installation, destructive operation, Git action, publication, or deployment occurred.
